Can you spread germs before feeling sick?

Yes! Germs multiply inside you first before you feel sick — this incubation period can last several days, and you can already spread them to others even without symptoms.

Oo! Dumadami muna ang germs sa katawan bago ka magkaramdam — ang incubation period na ito ay maaaring ilang araw, at makakahawa ka na kahit wala ka pang sintomas.

Makatakod ka ba bisan wala ka pa masakit?

Oo! Modaghan una ang germs sa lawas ayha ka mobati og sakit — kining incubation period mahimong pipila ka adlaw, ug makatakod na ka bisan wala pa kay sintomas.

How does soap actually kill germs?

Soap doesn't just stick to germs — it breaks apart their fatty outer coat until they fall apart! Scrub for 20 seconds to give it time to work.

Hindi lang basta dumidikit ang sabon sa germs — sinisira nito ang panlabas na balot na taba hanggang madurog ang mga ito! Kuskusin ng 20 segundo para magtrabaho ito nang maayos.

Why can't we see germs?

Germs are so tiny you need a microscope to see them — even a clean-looking hand or table may still have germs, so washing and cleaning matter.

Bakit hindi natin nakikita ang mga germs?

Napakaliit ng germs kaya kailangan ng microscope para makita ito — kahit mukhang malinis ang kamay o mesa, maaaring may germs pa rin, kaya mahalaga ang paghuhugas at paglilinis.

Gamay kaayo ang mga germs mao nga kinahanglan og microscope aron makita — bisan tan-awon nga limpyo ang kamot o lamesa, mahimong adunay germs gihapon, busa importante ang paghugas ug paglimpyo.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: many stamens are fused together to form that tube
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the different ways that plants reproduce, such as pollination, seed production, and plant propagation
assignedReviews.reason: Stamen fusion is floral morphology; the card never describes pollination, seed production, or propagation.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: many stamens are fused together to form that tube
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe the outer parts of plants, such as leaves, roots, and stems and identify their role to get water and nutrients from the soil
assignedReviews.reason: Fused stamens are not leaves, roots, or stems taking water and nutrients from soil.

copy.en:
Does a gumamela have only one stamen?

It looks like one tube, so many think gumamela has just a single stamen — but actually many stamens are fused together to form that tube.
copy.tl:
Iisa lang ba ang stamen ng gumamela?

Mukhang iisang tubo ito, kaya akala ng marami ay iisa lang ang stamen ng gumamela — pero totoo, maraming stamen ang pinagsama-sama para mabuo ang tubong iyon.
copy.bis:
Usa ra ba ka stamen ang gumamela?

Morag usa ka tubo kini, mao nga daghan ang naghunahuna nga usa ra ka stamen ang gumamela — apan tinuod, daghang stamen ang gitapok aron mahimo kanang tubo.

assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the different ways that plants reproduce, such as pollination, seed production, and plant propagation
assignedReviews.reason: Naming the male part is adjacent to pollination; the card never describes pollen transfer, seed production, or propagation.

copy.tl: Sa gitna ng bulaklak ng gumamela ay may mahabang tubo na hawak ang mga stamen, ang bahaging lalaki ng bulaklak.
copy.bis: Sa tunga sa bulak sa gumamela adunay taas nga tubo nga nagkupot sa mga stamen, ang lalaki nga bahin sa bulak.

assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions the gut but does not identify any digestive system parts (mouth, gullet, stomach, small/large intestine) or describe how they work. It is about gut bacteria and diet, not the anatomy or function of the digestive system.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The food you eat changes which bacteria live and grow in your gut.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: using a labeled diagram, trace how food travels through the digestive tract and explain how different digestive processes work, including mechanical processing, secretion, digestion, absorption, and elimination
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not use a labeled diagram, trace food through the digestive tract, or explain digestive processes (mechanical processing, secretion, digestion, absorption, elimination). It only mentions gut bacteria, which is not the focus of this competency.

copy.en: The food you eat changes which bacteria live and grow in your gut.
copy.tl: Ang uri ng pagkaing kinakain mo ay nakakaapekto sa mga bakteryang dumarami sa iyong bituka.
copy.bis: Ang matang sa pagkaon nga imong kaonon makaapekto sa bakterya nga modaghan sa imong tinai.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Most bacteria living in our gut are actually helpful
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: recognize that some organisms consist of a single cell (unicellular) like in bacteria and some consist of many cells (multicellular) like in a human
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses that gut bacteria are helpful, but does not address the unicellular vs multicellular distinction or that bacteria are single-celled organisms. It shares the topic of bacteria but provides no direct instructional support for recognizing unicellular vs multicellular organisms.

copy.en:
Are all bacteria bad for you?

No! Most bacteria living in our gut are actually helpful, and we need them to stay healthy.
copy.tl:
Masama ba ang lahat ng bakterya?

Hindi! Karamihan sa mga bakteryang nakatira sa ating bituka ay nakakatulong pala at kailangan natin sila.
copy.bis:
Daotan ba tanang bakterya?

Dili! Kadaghanan sa bakterya nga nagpuyo sa atong tinai makatabang pala ug atong gikinahanglan sila.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Your gut and brain are always talking to each other through signals
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: use models, flow charts, diagrams, and simulations to explain how body systems work together, such as digestion and excretion
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions gut and brain communication, which touches on body systems working together, but the competency specifically requires using models, flow charts, diagrams, or simulations to explain how body systems work together. The card uses none of these representations and does not explain how the systems work together in the required manner.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Your gut and brain are always talking to each other through signals
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions the gut (digestive system) and brain, but it does not describe how the digestive system works, nor does it cover the muscular, skeletal, circulatory, or respiratory systems. It only states that gut bacteria can affect feelings, which is not a description of how any of the listed body systems work.

copy.en: Your gut and brain are always talking to each other through signals — that's why gut bacteria can actually affect how you feel!
copy.tl: Ang bituka at utak natin ay palaging nag-uusap sa pamamagitan ng mga signal — kaya nakakaapekto ang gut bacteria sa ating pakiramdam!
copy.bis: Ang atong tinai ug utok kanunayng nagkomunikar pinaagi sa mga senyales — mao nga makaapekto ang gut bacteria sa atong pamati!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Most of your gut microbes live in the large intestine, or colon
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify from pictures and labeled diagrams the parts of the digestive system as mouth, gullet, stomach, small intestine, and large intestine, and describe how they work
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions the large intestine/colon but does not identify digestive system parts from pictures or labeled diagrams, nor does it describe how the listed parts (mouth, gullet, stomach, small intestine, large intestine) work. The content is about gut microbes, not the digestive system anatomy/function required by the competency.

copy.en:
Where do most gut microbes live?

Most of your gut microbes live in the large intestine, or colon, where most of their helpful work happens.
copy.tl:
Saan nakatira ang karamihan ng mikrobyo sa bituka?

Karamihan sa mikrobyo sa bituka ay nakatira sa makapal na bituka o colon, kung saan nagaganap ang karamihan ng tulong nila sa atin.
copy.bis:
Asa nagpuyo ang kadaghanan sa mikrobyo sa tinai?

Kadaghanan sa mikrobyo sa tinai nagpuyo sa dako nga tinai o colon, diin nahitabo ang kadaghanan sa ilang tabang kanato.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the hard plate you see, the cuticle skin at the edge that protects it, and the little white half-moon called the lunula near the bottom
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes parts of a fingernail, an outer body part of a human (animal), but does not identify their role to move or to gather food as required by the competency. It only names structures without linking them to movement or food gathering.

copy.en: A nail has several parts: the hard plate you see, the cuticle skin at the edge that protects it, and the little white half-moon called the lunula near the bottom.
copy.tl: Ang kuko ay may iba't ibang bahagi: ang matigas na plato na nakikita mo, ang cuticle sa gilid na nagpoprotekta, at ang maliit na puting lunula na hugis-buwan sa ibaba.
copy.bis: Ang kuko adunay lain-laing bahin: ang gahi nga plato nga imong makita, ang cuticle sa kilid nga manalipod, ug ang gamay nga puti nga lunula nga porma-bulan sa ubos.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: those parts are dead with no nerves
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses dead hair/nails, but does not teach the characteristics of living things (grow, respond, reproduce). It only touches on the concept of living vs dead tissue, which is not the competency's focus.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Cutting hair or nails doesn't hurt
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about hair and nails, not about animal outer body parts (head, legs, wings) and their role in movement and food gathering. No support for this competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: those parts are dead with no nerves
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the difference between living and non-living things and give examples of each that can be found in the local environment
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions dead vs living parts, which is tangentially related to living/non-living distinction, but it does not describe the difference between living and non-living things or give examples from the local environment. It is not direct instructional support.

copy.en:
Why doesn't cutting your hair or nails hurt?

Cutting hair or nails doesn't hurt because those parts are dead with no nerves — but cut a nail too short and you'll feel it, since that reaches the living part!
copy.tl:
Bakit hindi masakit ang gupit ng buhok o kuko?

Hindi masakit ang gugupitin ang buhok o kuko dahil patay na ang mga bahaging iyon at walang nerves — pero masakit kung labis mong paikliin ang kuko dahil naaabot mo na ang buhay na bahagi!
copy.bis:
Nganong dili sakit ang pagputol sa buhok o kuko?

Dili sakit ang pagputol sa buhok o kuko kay patay na kadto nga bahin ug walay nerbiyos — apan sakit kon sobra nimo pamub-on ang kuko kay maabot na nimo ang buhing bahin!
